screen: maxT over stats.score z (legacy R4 Cox U, permutation variance), rejecting above the ceil((B+1)(1-alpha)) null order statistic (stats.threshold) calibrated at the same n and arm

simulator.label: ESTIMATE (sim)
simulator.outcomes: atlas.simulation: Weibull k=1.5 PH, scale tuned to the cohort event fraction, stratum reverse-KM censoring at the administrative horizon

empirical.label: ESTIMATE (plasmode)
empirical.outcomes: the real cohort's stratum Kaplan-Meier baseline raised to HR**z (planted PH), T past the curve censored; the same stratum reverse-KM censoring

bootstrap: patients drawn with replacement from the real 159; study i shares patients and seeds across arms
comparison: difference = sim - plasmode power; paired conservative >=95% bounds (atlas.runner.paired_interval); a sensitivity comparison: an interval containing zero means no difference detected, not equivalence
scope: Real data exists only at the full-tissue design (all regions, full core, no mis-calls), where re-imaging is the identity; this checks the simulator's outcome model and calibrated-threshold power against the real cohort's own survival curve, not the imaging-noise model.
limits: HR 2 per SD is the imposed model parameter: on the discrete KM baseline, S0(t) ** r imposes proportional negative-log survival; it is not a fitted Cox HR. Both arms plant SYNTHETIC outcomes on the same empirical source. Intervals condition on that source, the fitted models and the realised calibration thresholds; they exclude source-estimation and calibration-fitting uncertainty. The stratum marginal KM is assumed to be the feature-zero baseline, not an identified conditional baseline. Each arm is calibrated separately, so this compares two procedures under two outcome models; it does not validate transfer of the simulator's cutoff or observed real-world power. A difference interval containing zero means no difference was detected; it is not equivalence, and its width is not a detection-power calculation.
